findings.claim: A node with annotations but no compartments is sized as a standard node, so its stereotype text is drawn on top of the centred class name.
findings.evidence: SizeStandardNode only branches to SizeClassNode when `node.Compartments.Count > 0` (DefaultLayoutEngine.cs:436), so an annotation-only node gets standard sizing and no `label:centerY`. But the renderer still calls AppendClassCompartments when `node.Annotations.Count > 0` (line 151), which draws the first annotation at `pad + fontSize * 0.85` (line 318). With a min-height box, that is roughly the same baseline as the centred label, so the two overlap.

members.claim: Annotations are drawn whenever `node.Annotations.Count > 0`, but layout only takes the class-sizing path when `Compartments.Count > 0` (DefaultLayoutEngine.cs:436). A node that has a stereotype but no compartments (e.g. a bare `<<interface>>` class) is sized as a standard node: no header space is reserved for the annotation and `label:centerY` is never set, so the class name is drawn at the node's vertical center. The annotation baseline (`pad + 0.85*fontSize`) then lands almost on top of the class-name baseline (`Height/2 + 0.35*fontSize`). The two texts overlap and can spill out of the box. Sizing should use `SizeClassNode` when `Compartments.Count > 0 || Annotations.Count > 0`.

members.claim: Size annotation-only nodes using the class header layout
members.evidence: When a node has annotations but no compartments, the renderer now draws those annotations, but this condition leaves the node on the standard sizing path. Apply header sizing and positioning to annotation-only nodes as well.

findings.reason: For each rendered line from GetRenderedLabelLines, which splits on '\n' (line 188), the renderer advances lineBaseline, but currentY moves only one line height per label. Layout's Lines.Sum at DefaultLayoutEngine.cs:508 also counts one line per label, so the extra lines overlap the next entry and the node is too short.
findings.claim: A compartment label with more than one line overlaps the next entry and can spill past the node, because layout and renderer each reserve only one line per label.
findings.evidence: Layout sums `(l.FontSize ?? fontSize) * DefaultLabelLineHeight` once per Label (DefaultLayoutEngine.cs:508). The renderer writes every line from `GetRenderedLabelLines(line)` and advances `lineBaseline` for each (lines 353-357), but moves `currentY` by only one line height per Label (line 358). So the next entry starts on top of the second rendered line, and the node height does not cover the extra lines.

members.claim: A compartment `Label` whose text contains newlines (or has several `Lines`) is drawn as several baselines, each `lineFontSize*1.15` apart. However, `currentY` advances by only one line height per `Label`. The extra lines overlap the next entry, and the last ones can run past the next divider or the bottom of the node.
